To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DGK inhibition decreases ENaC function by increasing the production of phosphatidylinositides, which in turn inhibit ENaC.
DGK inhibition reduces ENaC activity through the control of PIP5KI activity, and that DGK inhibition increases airway surface liquid volume.
DGK inhibition reduces ENaC activity through the regulation of PI(4)P and PI(4,4)P2 levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mathematical analysis of the regulation of ENAC, an ion channel that plays a crucial role in cystic fibrosis, through a computational model that integrates the dynamics of phosphatidylinositols with the regulation of ENA.
the development of a novel computational approach that can be applied to the study of the complex regulation of ion channels by signaling lipids.
understanding the mechanisms of ENaC regulation, which are important for the design of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of CF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of the ENaC by DGK is mediated by PIP5KI and PA.
DGK inhibition reduces ENaC activity through the control of PIP5KI and PA production, which in turn regulates PI(4, 5)P2 and, consequently, ENaC.
DGK regulates ENaC through the control of PIP5KI activity by PA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DGK regulates ENaC through the control of the PIP5KI activity.
DGK regulates ENaC by controlling the production of PIP5KI, which in turn regulates ENaC.
the mathematical model of ENaC regulation by PI(4, 5)P2 and DGK can be used to explain the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inhibition of DGK is an effective strategy for the treatment of CF, because it reduces the production of PA and consequently the production of PI(4)P by PIP5KI and the activity of ENaC, which is regulated by PI(4, 5)P2.
the DGK-PI(4, 5)P2-ENaC axis is a promising target for the treatment of cystic fibrosis.
DGK activity, through the regulation of ENAC, is an important factor in the pathophysiology of CF.
